18 An aircraft travels at a constant velocity of 90 m s–1 in horizontal flight. The diagram shows the
horizontal forces acting on the aircraft.
drag
2400 N
thrust
The mass of the aircraft is 2000 kg.
What is the power produced by the thrust force?
A
1.8 × 105
W
B
2.2 × 105
W
C
1.8 × 106
W
D
2.0 × 106
W

hints: Notice the aircraft is in horizontal flight at constant velocity, so compare the forward thrust arrow with the $2400 \text{ N}$ drag arrow to find the thrust magnitude.
Recall that mechanical power from a force parallel to velocity is $P = Fv$, with $F$ in $\text{N}$, $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $P$ in $\text{W}$.
Multiply the balanced thrust force by $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and check the power of ten: $2400 \times 90$ is just over $2 \times 10^{5} \text{ W}$, while the $2000 \text{ kg}$ mass is not needed.
walkthrough: Identify horizontal equilibrium: velocity is constant at $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so resultant horizontal force is zero by Newton's first law.
Therefore forward thrust magnitude equals backward drag magnitude: $F_{thrust} = 2400 \text{ N}$. The $2000 \text{ kg}$ mass is extra information for horizontal power.
State the power rule for a force in the direction of motion: $P = Fv$.
Substitute values with units: $P = 2400 \text{ N} \times 90 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 216000 \text{ W}$.
Express to two significant figures as $2.2 \times 10^{5} \text{ W}$ and check units are $\text{W}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This uses $2000 \times 90$ and treats mass in $\text{kg}$ as if it were force in $\text{N}$. Power needs driving force, not mass.

B.explanation: At constant velocity thrust equals drag, so $P = 2400 \times 90 = 2.16 \times 10^{5} \text{ W}$.

C.explanation: This is approximately weight times velocity, $2000 \times 9.81 \times 90$. Weight acts vertically and does no work in horizontal flight.

D.explanation: This is an order of magnitude too large and does not follow from $P = Fv$ with $F = 2400 \text{ N}$ and $v = 90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
